rows.analysis: 此字為現代醫學與化學名詞，由古柯樹名 coca 加上化學鹼類字尾 -ine 構成。源自奇楚瓦語 coca，經西班牙語進入英語，指從古柯葉中提煉出的強效中樞神經興奮劑。
rows.definition: 1. A powerful and addictive stimulant drug made from the leaves of the coca plant.

example.eng: The police seized a large shipment of cocaine at the port.
example.ch: 警方在港口查獲了一大批古柯鹼。

rows.analysis: 此字經由中古英語直接借自古法語 cofin，最終源自拉丁語 cophinus（意為籃子、箱子），其希臘語原義為編織的籃子。歷史上語義從「籃子」轉變為「裝屍體的容器」。
rows.definition: 1. A long, narrow box in which a dead body is buried or cremated.

example.eng: The wooden coffin was lowered slowly into the grave.
example.ch: 木製棺材緩緩降入墓穴中。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 cognitus（動詞 cognoscere「知道、認識」的過去分詞）加上形容詞字尾 -ive 構成。現代主要用於心理學與醫學領域，指與思考、記憶、理解等心智活動有關的。
rows.definition: 1. Connected with mental processes of understanding, learning, and remembering.

example.eng: Readiness for school involves developing basic cognitive skills.
example.ch: 入學準備包括發展基本的認知能力。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 co-（共同）加上 haerere（黏在一起）形成的動詞短語，再轉為現在分詞性質的形容詞。基本義為「黏合在一起的」，引申出邏輯連貫、條理分明或前後一致的現代義。
rows.definition: 1. Logical and well-organized, making it easy to understand; 2. United and working together effectively.

example.eng: She was able to present a coherent argument for the new policy.
example.ch: 她能夠就這項新政策提出條理清晰的論點。

example.eng: The various departments must form a coherent team.
example.ch: 各個部門必須組成一個協調一致的團隊。

rows.analysis: 由字首 con-（共同）加上動詞 incidere（偶然發生、落下，由 in- 加 cadere「落下」複合而成），再加上名詞字尾 -ence 構成。原意為「同時發生」，演變為指事情巧合地同時碰在一起。
rows.definition: 1. A situation in which striking things happen at the same time by chance, without any causal connection.

example.eng: It was pure coincidence that we met in Paris.
example.ch: 我們在巴黎相遇純粹是個巧合。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 collaborate 加上名詞字尾 -ion 構成。collaborate 源自拉丁語 com-（共同）加上 laborare（工作）。指共同參與一項工作或計畫，在特定政治語境下也指與敵對勢力合作。
rows.definition: 1. The action of working with someone to produce something; 2. Traitorous cooperation with an enemy.

example.eng: The book was written in close collaboration with his colleagues.
example.ch: 這本書是在與同事的密切合作下寫成的。

example.eng: He was accused of collaboration with the occupying forces.
example.ch: 他被指控與佔領軍通敵。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 collect 的拉丁語源 colligere（com- + legere「收集」）衍生出 collective，再加上形容詞字尾。指由群體共同擁有、進行或產生的特質。
rows.definition: 1. Done or shared by all members of a group of people.

example.eng: The decision was the result of a collective effort.
example.ch: 這個決定是集體努力的結果。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 collect 加上表示人的名詞字尾 -or 構成。指從事收集物品（如藝術品、郵票）的人，或負責收取款項、稅金的人員。
rows.definition: 1. A person who collects things of a particular type as a hobby or job; 2. A person whose job is to collect money, taxes, or tickets.

example.eng: He is a famous collector of antique clocks.
example.ch: 他是著名的古董鐘錶收藏家。

example.eng: The ticket collector checked our passes before we boarded.
example.ch: 驗票員在我們上車前檢查了我們的通行證。

rows.analysis: 由名詞 colony（源自拉丁語 colonia「農場、聚居地」）加上形容詞字尾 -al 構成。指與殖民地、殖民統治或殖民時期歷史相關的。
rows.definition: 1. Connected with or belonging to a country that controls another country.

example.eng: Many African nations gained independence from colonial rule in the 20th century.
example.ch: 許多非洲國家在20世紀贏得了擺脫殖民統治的獨立。

rows.analysis: 由名詞 column（報紙專欄、柱子）加上表示從事某職業者的字尾 -ist 構成。指在報紙或雜誌上定期撰寫固定專欄文章的作家。
rows.definition: 1. A journalist who writes a regular column for a newspaper or magazine.

example.eng: She is a political columnist for a major daily newspaper.
example.ch: 她是一家主要日報的政治專欄作家。

rows.analysis: 源自中古法語 combat，動詞為 combatre，由拉丁語 com-（共同）加上 battuere（打、擊）。作為名詞時指武裝衝突、軍事交戰或激烈的爭鬥。
rows.definition: 1. Fighting between armed forces or a struggle against something.

example.eng: Several soldiers were wounded in combat.
example.ch: 幾名士兵在戰鬥中受傷。

rows.analysis: 由希臘語 kōmōidia（喜劇）經拉丁語演變為 comedy，再結合名詞字尾 -an 構成。指以逗樂觀眾、表演喜劇或脫口秀為職業的人。
rows.definition: 1. An entertainer whose job is to make people laugh by telling jokes or funny stories.

example.eng: The stand-up comedian had the audience in stitches.
example.ch: 這位單口喜劇演員逗得觀眾捧腹大笑。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 comment（評論、解說）加上名詞字尾 -ary 構成。原意為對文本的解釋或註釋，現代廣泛用於體育賽事的實況解說或對社會時事的分析評論。
rows.definition: 1. A spoken or written description of an event as it happens; 2. Expressed opinions or critical explanations on an event or text.

example.eng: The football match had brilliant commentary by the veteran broadcaster.
example.ch: 這場足球賽由資深主播進行了精彩的實況轉播解說。

example.eng: His latest book offers a sharp commentary on modern politics.
example.ch: 他的最新著作對現代政治提出了犀利的評論。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 commentate（發表評論、擔任解說）加上表示人的字尾 -or 構成。指專門負責體育賽事、新聞事件實況解說或撰寫時事評論的人。
rows.definition: 1. A person who describes a sports event live on TV or radio, or who writes analytical news articles.

example.eng: The sports commentator predicted that the home team would win.
example.ch: 體育評論員預測主隊會獲勝。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 commissio（committere 的名詞形式，意為委託、送交），由 com-（共同、加強）與 mittere（送出）複合而成。引申出官方授權的委員會、商業上的仲介佣金及委託製作工作等義。
rows.definition: 1. An official group of people given a specific responsibility; 2. A payment given to an agent for selling goods; 3. An instruction or request to do something.

example.eng: The government has set up a commission to investigate the accident.
example.ch: 政府已成立一個委員會來調查這起事故。

example.eng: She earns a high commission on every house she sells.
example.ch: 她每賣出一棟房子就能賺取高額佣金。

example.eng: The artist received a commission to paint a mural.
example.ch: 這位藝術家接到了一份繪製壁畫的委託。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 commit 加上名詞字尾 -ment 構成。commit 源自拉丁語 committere（託付、交付）。名詞指對某項工作、組織或關係的莊嚴承諾、責任，或全心全意的投入。
rows.definition: 1. A promise or firm decision to do something; 2. The state of being dedicated to a cause or activity.

example.eng: I cannot make any financial commitments right now.
example.ch: 我目前無法做出任何財務承諾。

example.eng: Her success is due to her hard work and total commitment.
example.ch: 她的成功歸功於她的努力工作與全心投入。

rows.analysis: 源自中古法語 commodité，最終源自拉丁語 commoditas（便利、合適、利益），由 commodus（方便的、合適的）衍生而來。在經濟學中演變為指可自由買賣的基礎商品或農工原料。
rows.definition: 1. A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold; 2. A useful thing.

example.eng: Crude oil is a vital global commodity.
example.ch: 原油是至關重要的全球大宗商品。

example.eng: In a drought, clean water becomes a precious commodity.
example.ch: 乾旱期間，乾淨的水成了珍貴的資源。

rows.analysis: 由形容詞 common（共同的）的法語同源詞 commun，加上表示主義、學說的字尾 -ism 構成。指主張生產資料歸全社會公有、取消私有財產的政治與經濟思想體系。
rows.definition: 1. A political and economic system in which major property is publicly owned and each person works and is paid according to their abilities and needs.

example.eng: The collapse of the Soviet Union marked a major turning point for communism.
example.ch: 蘇聯的解體標誌著共產主義的一個重大轉折點。

rows.analysis: 由 communism 詞根加上表示人的字尾 -ist 構成，指信仰共產主義或加入共產黨的人。
rows.definition: 1. A supporter or member of a communist party or political system.

example.eng: He joined the communist party in his youth.
example.ch: 他在年輕時加入了共產黨。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 commutare（徹底改變、交換），由 com- 與 mutare（改變）複合而成。原意為交換或減輕刑罰，後來在美國鐵路語境中引申出「定期購買月票交換乘車」，最終演變為現代的「通勤」義。
rows.definition: 1. To travel some distance between one's home and place of work on a regular basis.

example.eng: He commutes to work by train every day.
example.ch: 他每天搭火車通勤上班。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 commute 加上表示人的名詞字尾 -or 構成，指每天固定往返於居住地與工作地點之間的人。
rows.definition: 1. A person who travels some distance to work on a regular basis.

example.eng: The morning train was packed with tired commuters.
example.ch: 早上的火車擠滿了疲憊的通勤族。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 compactus（compingere 的過去分詞，意為緊密結合），由 com-（共同）與 pangere（緊閉、固定）複合而成。形容物體結構緊密、節省空間或短小精幹。
rows.definition: 1. Closely and neatly packed together; smaller than normal; 2. Dense or solid.

example.eng: The apartment is small, but its layout is very compact.
example.ch: 這間公寓很小，但佈局非常緊湊。

example.eng: Soil that is too compact can prevent roots from growing.
example.ch: 過於緊實的土壤會阻礙根系生長。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 compare（比較）加上形容詞字尾 -able（可……的）構成。指性質相似、規模相當，因而能夠拿來互相比較的。
rows.definition: 1. Able to be likened to another; similar in size, amount, or quality.

example.eng: The two situations are not really comparable.
example.ch: 這兩種情況其實不具可比性。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 compassio，由 com-（共同）與 pati（承受、受苦，即 suffer）複合而成。字面義為「共同受苦」，引申為對他人痛苦感同身受並試圖給予幫助的同情心。
rows.definition: 1. Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.

example.eng: The nurse treated the sick patients with great compassion.
example.ch: 護士以極大的同情心照料生病的患者。

rows.analysis: 由名詞 compassion 加上形容詞字尾 -ate 構成，用來形容人富有同情心、體諒並關懷他人痛苦的特質。
rows.definition: 1. Feeling or showing sympathy and concern for others.

example.eng: She is a compassionate leader who always listens to her staff.
example.ch: 她是一位富有同情心的領導者，總是傾聽員工的心聲。

rows.analysis: 源自中古拉丁語 compatibilis，由 com-（共同）與 pati（承受、忍受）結合而成。原意為「能共受痛苦的」，現代引申為理念契合、軟硬體相容或能和平共處的。
rows.definition: 1. Able to exist or occur together without conflict; 2. Able to be used together, especially in computers.

example.eng: Their personalities are not compatible, so they often argue.
example.ch: 他們的個性不合，所以經常爭吵。

example.eng: This software is not compatible with your operating system.
example.ch: 這個軟體與你的作業系統不相容。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 compellere，由 com-（加強語氣）與 pellere（推、驅趕）複合而成。字面義為「強力驅使」，現代指法律、情勢或壓力迫使某人不得不做某事。
rows.definition: 1. To force someone to do something; to bring about by force.

example.eng: The bad weather compelled us to cancel the trip.
example.ch: 惡劣的天氣迫使我們取消了行程。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 compensatus（compensare 的過去分詞），由 com-（共同）與 pensare（稱重、衡量）複合而成。原意為「秤平、平衡」，現代演變為給予金錢補償或以其他優點彌補不足。
rows.definition: 1. To give something, usually money, to someone in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury; 2. To make up for something unwelcome.

example.eng: The airline compensated passengers for the delayed flight.
example.ch: 航空公司就航班延誤對乘客進行了賠償。

example.eng: Hard work can compensate for a lack of natural talent.
example.ch: 努力工作可以彌補天賦的不足。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 compensate 加上名詞字尾 -ion 構成。指因損失、受傷或工作勞動而獲得的金錢補償、賠償金或員工薪資福利報酬。
rows.definition: 1. Something, typically money, awarded to someone in recognition of loss or suffering; 2. Remuneration received for working.

example.eng: He demanded financial compensation for the damage to his car.
example.ch: 他要求對汽車損壞給予經濟賠償。

example.eng: The job offers a competitive salary and excellent compensation.
example.ch: 這份工作提供具競爭力的薪資與優渥的福利報酬。

rows.analysis: 由形容詞 competent 的拉丁語源 competentia（適合、對應）演變而來。指一個人勝任某項工作或處理特定事務的知識、技能與專業能力。
rows.definition: 1. The ability to do something successfully or efficiently.

example.eng: The test is designed to measure linguistic competence.
example.ch: 這項測試旨在衡量語言能力。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 competens（competere 的現在分詞，意為相稱、符合、有能力），由 com- 與 petere（追求、到達）複合而成。形容人具備足夠的技能與資格來把事情做好。
rows.definition: 1. Having the necessary ability, knowledge, or skills to do something successfully.

example.eng: She is a highly competent manager who handles crises well.
example.ch: 她是一位能力極強的經理，能妥善處理危機。

rows.analysis: 由形容詞 complex（複雜的，源自拉丁 complectere「編織在一起」）加上名詞字尾 -ity 構成。指事物因包含眾多互相交織的元素而產生的複雜狀態或特性。
rows.definition: 1. The state of being difficult to understand because of many involved parts.

example.eng: We must not underestimate the complexity of the problem.
example.ch: 我們絕不能低估這個問題的複雜性。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 comply 加上名詞字尾 -ance 構成。指依從法規、命令、標準或他人要求的行為與狀態。
rows.definition: 1. The act of obeying an order, rule, or request.

example.eng: The company was fined for non-compliance with environmental laws.
example.ch: 該公司因未遵守環保法規而被罰款。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 complicate（使複雜）加上名詞字尾 -ion 構成。原意為使事情糾結在一起的狀態，引申為突發的麻煩、難題，或醫學上的病情併發症。
rows.definition: 1. A circumstance that makes a situation more complex or difficult; 2. A secondary disease or condition aggravating an existing one.

example.eng: Unforeseen financial complications delayed the project.
example.ch: 未預見的財務難題耽誤了該專案。

example.eng: He developed serious lung complications after the surgery.
example.ch: 他在手術後出現了嚴重的肺部併發症。

rows.analysis: 源自義大利語 complimento 或法語 compliment，最終源自拉丁語 complere（填滿、完成）。原意為禮節性的致意或禮物，現代專指對他人的外表、能力或表現給予的讚賞詞句。
rows.definition: 1. A polite expression of praise or admiration.

example.eng: Thank you for the compliment on my cooking.
example.ch: 謝謝你誇獎我的手藝。

rows.analysis: 源自十六世紀義大利語 complire 或拉丁語 complere（圓滿完成、使滿足）。歷史上語義轉為「迎合他人意願」或「符合規章制度」，現代固定搭配介系詞 with 使用。
rows.definition: 1. To act in accordance with a wish, command, or rule.

example.eng: All employees must comply with company safety regulations.
example.ch: 所有員工都必須遵守公司的安全規章。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 componens（componere 的現在分詞，意為組裝、組合），由 com- 與 ponere（放置）複合而成。字面義為「放在一起的東西」，指構成機械、系統或化學混合物的各個組成部分或零件。
rows.definition: 1. A part or element of a larger whole, especially in a machine or system.

example.eng: Microchips are a crucial component of modern computers.
example.ch: 微晶片是現代電腦至關重要的組件。

rows.analysis: 源自中古英語 compounen，源於古法語 compondre，最終源自拉丁語 componere（組合）。名詞指化學上的化合物、語言學中的複合詞，或是東亞殖民語境中被圍牆圈起來的住宅大院（可能受馬來語 kampong 影響）。
rows.definition: 1. A substance formed by chemical union of two or more elements; 2. A thing made up of two or more parts; 3. An enclosed area containing a group of buildings.

example.eng: Water is a chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
example.ch: 水是氫和氧的化合物。

example.eng: The embassy staff live inside a secure compound.
example.ch: 大使館員工住在一個安全的圍場大院內。

rows.analysis: 由拉丁語 comprehendere，由 com-（加強語氣）與 prehendere（抓住、握住）複合而成。字面義為「心智上完全抓牢」，引申為徹底理解、懂某個概念或狀況。
rows.definition: 1. To understand something fully; to grasp mentally.

example.eng: She could not comprehend the full scale of the disaster.
example.ch: 她無法理解這場災難的全部規模。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 comprehend 透過其過去分詞詞幹加上名詞字尾 -ion 構成。指心智上理解、吸收複雜資訊或語言文字的能力。
rows.definition: 1. The ability to understand something; complete understanding.

example.eng: Reading comprehension is a vital skill for language learners.
example.ch: 閱讀理解能力對語言學習者至關重要。

rows.analysis: 源自中古法語 compris（comprendre 的過去分詞，意為包含），最終源自拉丁語 comprehendere。指某個整體包含或由特定的部分所組成。
rows.definition: 1. To consist of; to be made up of; to include.

example.eng: The committee is comprised of five experts from various fields.
example.ch: 該委員會由來自各領域的五位專家組成。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 compromissum（雙方同意提交仲裁的裁決），由 com-（共同）與 promittere（承諾）複合而成。歷史上指雙方互相讓步以達成協議，現代指解決紛爭的妥協方案。
rows.definition: 1. An agreement or settlement of a dispute that is reached by each side making concessions.

example.eng: Neither side is willing to make a compromise.
example.ch: 雙方都不願意做出妥協。

rows.analysis: 由名詞 compulsion（強迫，源自 compellere）衍生出的形容詞字尾 -ory 構成。指依法律、法規或規定非做不可、不得抗拒的。
rows.definition: 1. Required by law or a rule; mandatory.

example.eng: Education is compulsory for children up to the age of sixteen in this country.
example.ch: 在這個國家，十六歲以下的兒童接受教育是義務性的。

rows.analysis: 源自中古英語 concelen，借自古法語 conceler，最終源自拉丁語 concelare，由 con-（加強語氣）與 celare（隱藏、藏匿）複合而成。指將物體藏起或將真相隱瞞不讓人知。
rows.definition: 1. To hide something carefully; to keep secret.

example.eng: He tried to conceal his disappointment behind a smile.
example.ch: 他試圖用微笑掩飾心中的失望。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 concedere，由 con-（加強語氣）與 cedere（退讓、走開）複合而成。字面義為「完全退讓」，演變為勉強承認事實、選舉中認輸，或在談判中讓步。
rows.definition: 1. To admit that something is true after first denying or resisting it; 2. To surrender or yield something.

example.eng: She finally conceded that she had made a mistake.
example.ch: 她終於承認自己犯了錯。

example.eng: The candidate conceded the election to his opponent.
example.ch: 這名候選人向對手承認競選失敗。

rows.analysis: 源自古法語 concevoir，最終源自拉丁語 concipere，由 con-（共同、加強）與 capere（抓取、容納）複合而成。原意為「在心中抓住、孕育」，演變為構思計畫、想像情境或女性受孕。
rows.definition: 1. To form a plan or idea in the mind; 2. To become pregnant.

example.eng: Engineers conceived a brilliant plan to build the bridge.
example.ch: 工程師們構思出一個建造這座橋樑的絕妙計畫。

example.eng: She found it difficult to conceive a child.
example.ch: 她發現自己很難懷孕。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 conceive 的拉丁語源 conceptio 演變而來。指心中形成的觀念、計畫的最初構思，或生物學上的受孕成胎過程。
rows.definition: 1. A mental plan or idea; an understanding of something; 2. The action of conceiving a child.

example.eng: People have different conceptions of freedom.
example.ch: 人們對自由有不同的觀念。

example.eng: Alcohol can harm the fetus at the moment of conception.
example.ch: 酒精在受孕那一刻就可能對胎兒造成傷害。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 condemnare，由 con-（加強語氣）與 damnare（宣判罪名、處罰）複合而成。原意為法律上的宣判定罪，現代廣泛用於公開嚴厲譴責某人或某事，或判定建築物危險不能居住。
rows.definition: 1. To express complete disapproval of, typically in public; 2. To sentence someone to a punishment, especially death.

example.eng: World leaders strongly condemned the terrorist attack.
example.ch: 世界各國領導人強烈譴責這起恐怖襲擊。

example.eng: The criminal was condemned to life imprisonment.
example.ch: 這名罪犯被判處無期徒刑。

rows.analysis: 源自拉丁語 conducere，由 con-（共同）與 ducere（引導）複合而成。動詞指引導方向、執行實驗調查、指揮樂團或管理業務；名詞則重音在前（/ˈkɑːndʌkt/），指品行行為（在此處依合約為動詞 row）。
rows.definition: 1. To guide or lead someone through a place; 2. To organize and carry out a particular activity.

example.eng: The guide will conduct us through the ancient museum.
example.ch: 導遊將帶領我們參觀這座古老的博物館。

example.eng: Scientists are conducting research on renewable energy.
example.ch: 科學家們正在進行有關renewable energy的研究。

rows.analysis: 由動詞 confess（源自拉丁語 confiteri，con- + fateri「坦白、承認」）加上名詞字尾 -ion 構成。指罪犯向警方招供罪行、個人坦承祕密，或天主教中的神聖告解。
rows.definition: 1. A formal statement admitting that one is guilty of a crime; 2. An admission of something one is ashamed of.

example.eng: The police obtained a signed confession from the suspect.
example.ch: 警方取得了嫌疑人簽字的招供書。

example.eng: He made a confession that he had lost all the money.
example.ch: 他坦白自己把所有的錢都輸光了。
